LEARN.TITLE: Learn the numbers
LEARN.LEDE: Numerology here works the simple way: you take a birth date and a name and add the digits together until there's one left. Each number then sits on two planets, the console's own Stavefall seat and its planet in the Vedic tradition. This page shows how the adding is done and where the two seatings come from.
COUNT: Add up the digits of a number. If you end up with two digits, add those together too, and keep going until there's only one. The one exception is 11, 22 and 33, which are master numbers and are left as they are.

Your life path uses your whole birth date. Reduce the month, the day and the year separately, then add the three together and reduce again. For 17 May 1990: the month is 5, the day 17 becomes 1 + 7 = 8, and the year 1990 becomes 1 + 9 + 9 + 0 = 19, then 1 + 9 = 10, then 1. That gives 5 + 8 + 1 = 14, and 1 + 4 = 5, so it's Life path 5.

Your birthday number is just the day of the month (the 17th gives 8). Your personal year swaps your birth year for the current year, so it changes every January. It tells you what kind of year you're in right now.
NAME: Use your full name at birth, every part of it, exactly as it was first written. Each letter has a number, counting through the alphabet in nines: A is 1 and I is 9, then J starts again at 1. Accents are dropped, and hyphens and apostrophes don't count.

Your expression number adds up every letter and shows what your name gives you to work with. Your soul urge adds up only the vowels (A, E, I, O, U, plus Y when a word has no other vowel) and shows what you really want. Your personality number adds up only the consonants and shows how people first see you. Reduce each part of the name on its own, then add the parts together and reduce once more. JOHN is 1 + 6 + 8 + 5 = 20, which is 2. SMITH is 1 + 4 + 9 + 2 + 8 = 24, which is 6. So John Smith's expression number is 2 + 6 = 8.
LEARN.MASTER: 11, 22 and 33 aren't reduced any further. They're stronger versions of 2, 4 and 6, with the same character turned up, and each one sits on the same planets as the number it comes from, so 11 sits where 2 does.
STAVEFALL: Stavefall doesn't borrow its numbers from an existing numerology tradition. It places them on the Planetary Ladder, the console's chain of seven stations running from the crown of the head down to the base of the spine, with one planet feeding each station.

Counting down from the crown, the Sun feeds the crown and takes 1, and the Moon feeds the brow and takes 2. The other five planets take 3 to 7 in the order the ladder already goes: Saturn at the throat, Jupiter at the heart, Mars at the solar plexus, Venus at the sacrum and Mercury at the root. The ladder follows its own rule here too, because from root to throat each planet takes longer to go round the Sun than the one below it (Mercury 88 days, Venus 225, Mars 687, Jupiter 4,333 and Saturn 10,759).

That covers seven numbers. The two nodes aren't stations. They're more like the pole the stations are threaded on, so they take the last two numbers. Rahu is 8, the pole above the crown, and Ketu is 9, the pole below the feet. Nine is where the counting starts over, which suits Ketu, the point where things fade away.
So a Stavefall number isn't just a planet. It's a whole station, with its own realm, place in the body, colour and tone.
VEDIC: Indian numerology, called Ank Jyotish, gives each number to one of the nine planets of Jyotish: 1 is the Sun, 2 the Moon, 3 Jupiter, 4 Rahu, 5 Mercury, 6 Venus, 7 Ketu, 8 Saturn and 9 Mars. This is the version most people will have come across before.
The two systems agree on 1, 2 and 6 (the Sun, the Moon and Venus) and differ on the rest.
LEARN.READ: When the two seatings agree, the number speaks with one voice and counts double. When they differ, you have two planets for one number. The Stavefall planet tells you where the number lives in the body and on the ladder, and the Vedic planet tells you which planet the tradition hears in it. Your reading looks for both in your own chart: which sign and house each one is in, and the years its period runs.
LEARN.DESC: A free guide to numerology in The Wyrd Console: how your life path, birthday, personal year and name numbers are counted, master numbers, and the two planets each number sits on, Stavefall and Vedic.

TITLE: The Numbers
SUB: your birth date and your name, counted
INTRO: Numerology is the simplest tool in the console. You take a birth date and a name and keep adding the digits together until you're left with one. Each number then sits on two planets: its Stavefall seat, which is the console's own, and its planet in the Vedic tradition. On its own a number is quite abstract, but once you can see where its planets sit in your chart and when their periods come, it starts to mean something.
NO_NAME: Add your full name at birth, exactly as it was first written, and three more numbers appear here: your expression, your soul urge and your personality.

KIND.life_path: the path your whole life follows
KIND.birthday: the gift you were born with
KIND.personal_year: the year you're in right now, {year}
KIND.expression: what your full name gives you to work with
KIND.soul_urge: what you really want, from the vowels in your name
KIND.personality: how other people first see you, from the consonants

1.name: the beginner
1.light: Starting things, going first, and standing on your own two feet without waiting to be told you can.
1.shadow: Finding it hard to follow anyone, and mistaking being alone for being independent.

2.name: the go-between
2.light: Partnership, tact, and seeing both sides of something clearly enough to bring them together.
2.shadow: Disappearing into other people, and waiting to be chosen instead of choosing.

3.name: the voice
3.light: Expression and creativity. Your life tends to find its way through speaking, writing, making or performing.
3.shadow: Spreading yourself across too many things, or performing a feeling instead of actually feeling it.

4.name: the builder
4.light: Building things properly: order, foundations, and steady work that's still standing years later.
4.shadow: Getting rigid, or using work as a place to hide.

5.name: the traveller
5.light: Freedom, change and experience. You learn by going out, trying things and coming back changed.
5.shadow: Restlessness, and leaving before you've dealt with the consequences.

6.name: the keeper
6.light: Taking care of things: the home, the people in it, and the small jobs nobody else notices. At its best that care is generous and steady.
6.shadow: Care that turns into control, or giving so much that you quietly resent it.

7.name: the seeker
7.light: Looking inward and studying deeply. Time on your own is where you find what's true.
7.shadow: Withdrawing too far, or getting suspicious and shutting people out.

8.name: the steward
8.light: Power, money and responsibility, handled fairly and with a steady hand.
8.shadow: Trying to control everything, or tipping things in your own favour.

9.name: the finisher
9.light: Completion and compassion. You see the bigger picture and help bring things to a close for other people.
9.shadow: Carrying everyone else's pain, or leaving before the job is finished.

11.name: the messenger
11.light: A stronger version of 2: sharp intuition, and a gift for carrying messages between people.
11.shadow: Nervous energy and overwhelm, when too much is coming in and there's nowhere to ground it.

22.name: the master builder
22.light: A stronger version of 4: a builder whose work can hold up a whole community, not just a household.
22.shadow: Plans so big they never get started.

33.name: the teacher
33.light: A stronger version of 6: caring for people in a way that teaches them to care for themselves.
33.shadow: Needing to rescue people in order to feel like yourself.
